question: WHY DO THE WINGTIPS
BEND UPWARDS?
options: To make the plane look modern
To stop the wings from shaking
answer_full: To save fuel – they are called winglets
recap: Many airliners have wingtips that bend sharply upwards into a small fin.
explain: The air under a wing has higher pressure than the air above it. At the tip, it curls around and spins into a big whirlwind, called a wingtip vortex.
That spinning air costs energy and holds the plane back. Engineers call it induced drag, and the engines have to burn extra fuel to make up for it.
The winglet weakens that vortex. That cuts fuel burn by up to around five percent, and across all airlines that adds up to billions of litres.
